interpretation: The observational premise of the second horn: the intermediate 'would not change, but now it is always seen to' (νῦν δʼ ἀεὶ φαίνεται). Read as what the observation states: change in respect of the contradictory pair is seen (STMT-CHANGE-IS-SEEN). The universal premise the formal argument uses, that every state of the domain starts such a change (STMT-WHAT-IS-ALWAYS-CHANGES), is stronger and is not attributed to this sentence: it is the formalization's own open premise.
